true-crime-podcast-episodes-stranger-dan.headline: True Crime Podcast Episodes - Stranger Danger Myth - Episode Recs
true-crime-podcast-episodes-stranger-dan.author: altaralter
true-crime-podcast-episodes-stranger-dan.core: Posted in last 7 days True Crime Podcast Episodes - Stranger Danger Myth - Episode Recs true crime podcasts and the stranger danger myth: looking for episode recs TLDR: Looking for episodes from (popular/mainstream) true crime podcasts that reinforce the stranger danger myth for an article I am working on. Hi y'all! I'm a a journalist and I'm looking to write about how true crime podcasts often reinforce the stranger danger myth and contribute to hyper vigilance and paranoia that is then used to legitimize excessive policing and mass incarceration. I used to be an avid true crime podcast listener, but as a I learned more about police misconduct and crime statistics, I stopped being able to stomach them. I've seen a rise of women on social media talking about how they never go out alone and generally express paranoia at being out in public, especially at night, believing they might be kidnapped/killed/assaulted/etc, when statistically, if any of those things happened to them, the most likely perpetrator (by a wide margin) is a current or former romantic partner. Basically, I'm arguing that true crime podcasts have made (white) women exceedingly hyper-vigilant (despite overwhelming evidence that crime is at an all time low and the odds of being attacked by a stranger are minimal) and how this serves to reinforce patriarchal notions (women shouldn't be independent, women should stay in the home) and carceral notions (police make us safe, prison is an effective way to prevent crime and rehabilitate criminals) I remember being given "tips" about how not to end up in the situations the (often white female) victims ended up in and other than being kinda victim blame-y, I just found the idea that I need to be planning my life around the minuscule probability that a stranger would attempt to murder me to be irrational and exhausting. I remember Crime Junkie doing this a lot, but if anyone could point me to any podcasts episodes that push the stranger danger myth, I'd greatly appreciate it! PS: I won't be engaging with any arguments against my thesis, as I am still in the research phase. I don't want to create a forum for us to discuss the effectiveness of police or the help/harm of TC podcasts. Crime Junkie

airline-pilots-and-flight-attendants-cab.author: David C Forward
airline-pilots-and-flight-attendants-cab.core: Posted in last 7 days Airline Pilots & Flight Attendants - Cabin Fume Events 📚 Second-Time Sundays: a story from the Stories from Seat 4A archive. The captain was slumped forward, eyes half-closed. The first officer was losing consciousness too. At 18,000 feet over Massachusetts, a Spirit Airlines A319 was descending toward Boston, and both pilots had been poisoned by the air they were breathing. First Officer Eric Tellman got his oxygen mask on just in time, and landed the plane alone, his memory of the flight already slipping away. He never flew again. The industry calls it an “odor incident.” Crews call it a fume event. On almost every jet except the Boeing 787, cabin air is drawn straight off the engines, and when an oil seal leaks, the air can carry vaporized engine oil containing a known neurotoxin. It happens more often than you might think. By one FAA-funded estimate, roughly one flight in every 5,000. I first published this investigation in April, when few people were reading. It deserves a second look. You'll find the link in the comment below and for a limited time only, we are giving away FREE subscriptions. Sign up as a free subscriber and get every new story in your email box every Tuesday. If you’re crew and you’ve experienced a fume event, I’d like to hear from you. #SecondTimeSundays #AviationSafety #CabinAir

western-massachusetts-artists-and-reside.core: Posted in last 7 days Western Massachusetts Artists & Residents - Stories About Home Five months ago, I walked across across a stage at Principia College in a black gown and a cap that barely stayed on my braided hair, to the cheers of friends, families, and professors, who had somehow survived having me in their classes. On the other side of that stage was a question I didn't quite have an answer to: What comes next? Soon enough, my friends and I scattered across the map. Some landed in Washington, most stayed in Illinois (for now), and I headed east to Massachusetts. There, I traded college assignments for deadlines as a culture writer for The Christian Science Monitor. But it hasn't all been roses. Some days feel like a dry spell, spent staring at a blank document and wondering where the words have gone. Other days feel too short, with stories unfolding and the right words coming together in harmony. On those quieter days, I've sometimes questioned whether I chose the right path. But the people around me have always found ways to shut those doubts through their trust, encouragement, and unwavering support. And then there are the stories that remind me just how much I enjoy what I do. Recently, I wrote about a western Massachusetts artist whose album explores an intriguing question: What makes a place home? Is it the place itself, or the people we find there? It's one of a growing list of culture stories I've enjoyed exploring since joining the Monitor. I'm grateful for the opportunity to keep learning and telling stories about the people, ideas, and cultures shaping our world. And if you know of interesting people, communities, or cultural experiences worth exploring, don't hesitate to reach out. I'd love to hear from you. Here’s a link to the full story: https://lnkd.in/e_b37-w4 The Christian Science Monitor

sound-artists-and-field-recordists-run-r.author: Run_Radio
sound-artists-and-field-recordists-run-r.core: Posted in last 7 days Sound Artists & Field Recordists - RUN RADIO Aarhus Open Call OPEN CALL: RUN RADIO, a music radio + sound archive in Aarhus, DK, wants your field recordings, mixes, sound art, audio docs and more Hi all! I run RUN RADIO\\,\\ a music radio and sound archive/research space in Aarhus, Denmark, in collaboration with the culture and music space Institute for X. We’re looking for a really diverse range of audio projects and would love to hear from you. What we’re looking for: Field recordings Live music recordings (a concert you or someone else performed, perhaps?) Sound art projects Audio documentaries DJ mixes/playlists For researches and archivist, submit a curation of your discoveries, such as audio clips from interviews, movies, cartoons and TV series etc. The more niche, weird and out there, the better. For musicians, we’re open to original music, but since we’re more interested in curation, you could make a mix with your own music alongside references, inspirations, behind the scenes studio recordings, or you talking about the project. If you’d rather not, send us your album and we’ll pick songs for a future mix and make sure to hype you up when we schedule it. If you're more of a radio host, you can send us recordings of a show you've made as long as it is focused on music and not more of a podcast. How to submit? Email [email redacted] with a downloadable transfer link (SwissTransfer or Google Drive preferred) and include in the email body: Full name and/or artist name, pronouns and location Content type (mix, field recording, interview clip, etc.) Title: a creative one, or simply “mixtape by \[your name\]” Track list / source list (required for mixes and playlists) An image for the broadcast, but no selfies please (we’ll add one if you don’t send one) A short description: what is it, what should we know, what does it mean to you? Your social links Specs Audio files: MP3 320kbps Mixes and playlists: 30 to 90 mins Field recordings: 20 to 60 mins All other content types: no duration limits Link and source anything and everything you can You can submit multiple files, multiple times NO AI! By submitting, you agree you are happy to share this content with us and that we have your permission to broadcast, curate it how we see fit and rebroadcast in the future. You maintain ownership of your work and we will always credit you. We will only broadcast content live and there are currently no plans to archive anything online (we are archiving internally) which is a big aspect of this project. However, this may change in the future. We want to move away from streaming on demand and move towards listening with intention. This is something to keep in mind if you want work together. Please comment or email with questions! IG \_garane or instituteforx

adults-18-with-parkinsons-beyond-roar-st.core: Posted in last 7 days Adults 18+ With Parkinson's - Beyond Roar Story Series 👀🦁 RIGHT THEN… I’VE BEEN PLOTTING SOMETHING! You’ve heard enough about me and my Parkinson’s journey… 😂 Now I want to hear about YOU! Over the past year I’ve met some genuinely incredible people. Different ages, backgrounds, cultures, experiences… all connected in some way through Parkinson’s. And it’s got me thinking. We talk loads about the condition.
